narrative:
The model estimated a 41% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain, but it is high enough to exceed the bank’s approval threshold, so your application was denied.

The strongest factor was your checking account status: your account is currently below zero. Only about 12.6% of approved applicants have this status, compared with 59.2% who have no checking account recorded, so a negative balance was treated as a significant sign of financial strain. This factor pushed the decision toward bad credit more than any other.

Two other factors worked in your favor. Your installment rate is only 1% of disposable income, far below the approved average of about 3%, suggesting repayments should be manageable. Your requested amount of 2,039 DM is also below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, which reduced the risk assessment. However, these favorable points were not enough to offset the concern raised by your checking account.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account into a positive or at least non-negative position and keeping it there for several months. You could also provide recent statements showing stable balances or savings, and speak with the bank about whether a smaller loan, a guarantor, or a later reapplication would be considered.
